shared_elements: upright stone monolith carved in low relief
vertical stacking of motifs into registers/zones
curving serpentine or hook-like forms in the lower zone
schematic arms/limbs rendered as bent linear elements
repeated small motifs forming a band across the upper part
heavily weathered stone surface with shallow outlined carving
justification: Both are weathered upright stone blocks bearing shallow relief organised in stacked horizontal zones, with a band of small repeated motifs above and larger curling, serpentine or beaked forms filling the lower field — that vertical zoning is the most specific correspondence. Otherwise they differ sharply: A is a flat-faced rectangular pillar with crisply outlined, well-spaced animal silhouettes in clear profile, while B is a rounded boulder covered by a dense, interlocking, frontally-oriented composition of curvilinear abstracted forms with rounded modelling rather than incised silhouette.
